explained.headline: Bank of England raises interest rates to 4%

happened.text: Eight members of the Bank's monetary policy committee voted for the move, while Catherine Mann preferred a half-point increase.

background.text: The monetary policy committee sets interest rates to keep price rises at a steady level.
The Middle East conflict has driven oil prices persistently above $100 in recent months, following a failure to reopen the strait of Hormuz.

matters.text: About 500,000 homeowners with mortgages tracking the Bank of England rate face immediate increases in monthly repayments.
The Bank of England expects United Kingdom inflation to rise to 4.9% in the middle of next year.

uncertain.text: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey raised the prospect of another rate rise in the near future, stating that a resolution to the Iran conflict is the key factor.
An additional 500,000 homeowners on standard variable rates must wait to see if lenders choose to pass on the rate rise.

terms.definition: The official interest rate set by a central bank to influence borrowing and lending across the economy.
The default interest rate a mortgage lender charges once an initial fixed-term or tracker deal ends.
